items.title: Vanishing of the generic-triviality kernel for torsors under a quasi-split reductive group over an essentially smooth algebra over a semilocal Prüfer domain, in the generic-fibre case and in Krull-dimension-one
items.difficulty_reason: Auslander's flatness criterion, purity for reductive torsors and the Grothendieck-Serre conjecture are all stated over Noetherian, regular or Dedekind bases and none can be applied here, so the paper re-proves Auslander's criterion over a valuation ring via a new length function on finitely presented torsion modules (4.3, printed 211-212) and a two-case indiction on (ht(s), d_x) (4.8, printed 213-216), re-establishes purity for reflexive sheaves over regular coherent rings (2.19, 2.21, 2.22, printed 201-204), does the codimension bookkeeping fibrewise over Spec R (3.2, 3.5, printed 205-207) — which is what forces dim R = 1 in clause (ii) — and supplies the missing reductive inputs through the toral purity 7.9 and toral Grothendieck-Serre 7.11 (printed 233-234). The retained statement's own proof at native 2330-2332 is three lines precisely because the whole difficulty sits in that machinery plus the three curve replacements 8.5-8.7. The author records that clause (ii) generalises the main result of Ces22a and clause (i) is a Prüferian version of the Nisnevich conjecture inspired by Ces22b's Dedekind case; neither of those works is in this corpus, and the base-class change invalidates their proofs, so the research-level content is carried by this paper's own printed 210-216 and 227-240. Recorded in full in DIFFICULTY_SCREENING.json, including the fifteen numbered positions that carry no proof environment and the disposition of each.

dedup.scope: Exact identity probe on four DOI spellings plus title/phrase probes inside the stored native TeX bodies, with the matched sentence read in each neighbour body. No row in sources/problems/works is keyed to this DOI; no neighbour states the retained result or a case of it. The four Prüfer spellings return 0 rows, so the base class of the retained theorem does not occur in the corpus at all. The three closest rows (Stacks 0EA4, 0BMA and Nagata purity of branch locus) state the classical phenomena over regular or locally Noetherian bases, which is exactly the hypothesis the retained theorem removes.

standard_prerequisites: Bertin's notion of regularity for coherent rings as finite projective dimension of every finitely generated ideal, and its agreement with the Noetherian notion by Serre's homological characterisation (native 288-301, citing Ber71, Ber72, Ser56)
the Auslander-Buchsbaum formula in the Noetherian case (native 291, AB57 Th. 3.7) and purity for reductive torsors over regular local rings of dimension two (native 294-295, CTS79 Th. 6.13)
fppf descent for torsors and the standard theory of reductive group schemes with Borel subgroups and quasi-pinnings (SGA3IIInew Exp. XXVI)
the valuative criterion of properness and the limit/approximation machinery for filtering a semilocal Prüfer domain by finite-dimensional subrings (8.3 and 3.4, the latter \cf GL23 Lem. 2.2)
these are cited accurately and not re-proved here, in accordance with the rule that standard prerequisites may be cited without recursive re-proof
core_obligations: reproduce the exact two clauses of Theorem 8.1 with the hypotheses as written: semilocal Prüfer R, integral semilocal essentially smooth R-algebra A, quasi-split reductive A-group G, and the additional dim R = 1 in clause (ii) only
carry the authentic author proof at native 2330-2332 and the full reduction chain 8.2-8.7, including the geometrically-unibranch case of 8.4 whose Noetherian hypothesis the author records as unused

do not substitute the classical Noetherian or Dedekind proofs of Auslander's criterion, of purity for reductive torsors, or of Grothendieck-Serre for the Prüferian arguments of printed 210-216 and 227-234
keep the fibrewise codimension conditions over Spec R distinct from a single global codimension condition, and keep the two clauses' kernels distinct
cite the external inputs with the paper's own locators and do not claim their proofs
record, not repair, the literal departures of the author's file
